subject: Combining data from different survey methods

messages.author: 0045bcc09587a46f
messages.subject: Combining data from different survey methods
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’m carrying out an analysis of lion density using two data sets: camera trap data from a camera trap survey, and direct sightings data from a search-encounter survey. Both the surveys were carried out in the same area and during the same period.

In addition to comparing the separate density estimates produced through these two survey types, I'd like to try and combine the different data types into a single model. This is because I expect it should improve my density estimate (by virtue of increasing the number of captures and recaptures), and more broadly because I think it could be a useful approach in certain contexts, and would like to work out how (if!) it can be done.

I’ve already modelled both these datasets separately in secr. For the camera trap data, I used proximity detectors with binary effort. For the search encounter data, I converted the study area into a 1x1km grid of cells, with effort calculated as the number of kilometres driven in that cell on that day – this means it is also proximity detector type, but with a different (non-binary) measure of effort.

I know that there is currently no function to pool capthist data from different detector arrays, and that it is recommended to merge the input files and rebuild the capthist object from scratch. However, is it possible to do this with two different survey methods with different measures of effort (binary and non-binary)?

Otherwise it would be possible to use a binary measure of effort for the search encounter data (i.e. 1 if that pixel was surveyed on that sampling occasion, 0 if it was not) and combine it with the camera trap data into a single set of input files. However, the actual effort is really quite different between the two data types, so this seems like it may not be a good way forward.

Any advice would be much appreciated!

Thanks,
Charlotte

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Combining data from different survey methods
parts:
'binary.usage' is an argument of read.traps that has no downstream effect, as I remember. Once upon a time, all 'usage' data were binary, then the capability expanded (the code in read.traps from 2012 is still marked as 'tentative'!). 'binary.usage' merely switches between old and new input code blocks. The usage matrix of a traps object can mix binary and non-binary.

So I suggest you simply enter the trap- and occasion-specific values together with binary.usage = FALSE. Use only spaces, not commas (until a fix I have just applied on GitHub percolates through to another CRAN version of secr).

Of course, you will need to model differing detection parameters.

Murray

Thanks so much, it's good to know it's fine to combine binary and non-binary effort - I combined the input files and ran the models with survey type as a detection covariate, and it all seemed to work as expected.

Out of interest, what is the issue with using csv versus space delimited input files? Is this an issue specific to these data (mixture of binary and non-binary), or do you generally recommend spaces over commas for all secr input files?

Thanks,
Charlotte

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Combining data from different survey methods
parts:
The format for effort codes was designed originally to allow a string of zeros and ones e.g. 011011. Obviously that wasn't going to work for non-binary effort, so space-separated fields were allowed. More recently, csv input has become common so the format needed to catch up. I don't know right off whether commas are a problem elsewhere, but if you don't need csv it probably is safer to avoid them.
Murray
